sections.skill: Give an informal argument for volume formulas

questions.skill: Give an informal argument for volume formulas
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Explain why the volume of a cylinder is the area of its base times its height.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why the volume of a cylinder is the area of its base times its height.
questions.correct_answer: The cylinder is a stack of equal circles (cross sections) with area πr²; stacking them to height h gives πr² · h.

questions.skill: Give an informal argument for volume formulas
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 9 as a first forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A straight stack of coins and a slanted stack have the same coins and the same height. Do they have the same volume? Explain.
questions.prompt_markup:
A straight stack of coins and a slanted stack have the same coins and the same height.
Do they have the same volume? Explain.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. At every height the cross sections have the same area (Cavalieri's principle).
